name: TextField
purpose: Let a user write or edit a single line of free text.
intent: Provide one consistent, accessible native text-input control - sizing, borders, and interaction states - that every free-text entry point in the product shares. Composes an optional leading icon/text slot and an optional trailing icon/action slot (which may itself compose a real Icon Button or Button), which is why it lives at the molecule tier rather than atom.

showCaret.note: Figma mockup-only, not a real prop.

placeholder.note: Figma mockup-only toggle between placeholder/value text, not a real prop.

elemBeforeInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the leading slot. Never interactive. The text case (e.g. a '$' currency prefix) is bound to fixed body-lg typography at every field size.

elemAfterInputComponent.note: Separate Figma component for the trailing slot. Frequently interactive (e.g. a clear action) - confirmed from a screenshot of the clear icon-button in its hover state. The icon-button case uses appearance=subtle, shape=square. A third `label` type was added later, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle) for compact metadata/status after the input (e.g. a unit or status pill) - confirmed directly from the component's own nested instance properties, not assumed. iconAfter is already typed React.ReactNode and .action is a plain centered flex wrapper, so a Label already renders correctly there with no component code changes.

apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's autofill state (added after this contract was first written; re-checked 2026-10-13 in both contexts) layers color/background/autofill/default over color/elevation/surface/raised/default and keeps each context's resting stroke (border/input 1px on context=default, none on context=inline). Code applies it on .root:has(.input:autofill), or the documentation-only data-force-state='autofill' pin, except when disabled: background-color raised-default plus the tint as a background-image layer, so context=inline also gets the raised surface. The tint is its own layer, so hover (which sets background-color only, never the background shorthand) and focus/invalid still apply while the field is autofilled - a combination Figma doesn't show. The browser's own !important autofill fill on the input is hidden with background-clip: text, and -webkit-text-fill-color/caret-color replace its forced text color. Not a long background-color transition: that needs a raw timing the motion rules don't allow, and switching it off for reduced motion would bring the browser's fill back. Not an inset box-shadow in the frame color either: that would have to follow every frame state.

Figma's 'state' axis (default/hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill) is not a real prop - verified from bound tokens: hover=:hover, focus=focus+empty (:focus-within + :placeholder-shown), typing=focus+has-value (:focus-within, not :placeholder-shown), filled=unfocused+has-value (not :placeholder-shown), autofill=:autofill on the input. All five derive from native pseudo-classes plus the input's own value; none are exposed as a prop.

Figma's 'context' axis (default/inline) is the 'context' prop - the same name and values. It replaces the earlier 'appearance' prop (default/subtle/inline), which is deprecated but still accepted: subtle and inline both map to context=inline, default to context=default. The old code-only appearance=inline look (subtle without the hover background) was merged into context=inline, so Key Value Pair inline fields now get Figma's hover background.
isInvalid renders with strokeWeight=2 even when not focused, confirmed directly from node data - invalid's thicker border is not a focus-only effect.

Figma's literal focus treatment thickens the frame's own border 1px->2px and swaps its color to --color-border-focus. Focus/typing replaces the resting border's color directly - the same pattern invalid already uses - rather than adding an outline ring around it, per explicit design feedback. Border width does not literally change to 2px, though: an earlier pass changed the real border-width on context=default's focus AND invalid, matching Figma directly, but that shifts the content box (and the placeholder/value text and typing caret) on every side, reported directly against the component from a side-by-side screenshot - both now paint the extra pixel via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--border-width-md) - var(--border-width-sm)) <color> instead, keeping border-width a constant 1px in the box model with zero layout impact.

Hover is suppressed once the field is focus/typing (:focus-within, or the pinned data-force-state='focus' reference) - hover should only ever be visible on an inactive field, per explicit design feedback.

showCaret and placeholder (BOOLEAN) component properties exist only to drive Figma's own mockup and have no code equivalent - a real input shows its own caret and switches placeholder/value automatically.

context=inline's bottom corners are always square (border-bottom-{left,right}-radius: 0), confirmed directly from Figma's per-corner radius data on the inline variants - only the top corners share context=default's radius.

context=inline rests at the same 1px bottom border-width context=default uses at rest, per explicit design feedback (an earlier pass reserved a constant 2px transparent border specifically to avoid a layout shift; that reservation was reverted). Reverting it reintroduced the shift a real border-width change causes (the vertically-centered text visibly nudges by a pixel), so focus/invalid on context=inline now paint the thicker look via box-shadow (inset 0 calc(-1 * (var(--border-width-md) - var(--border-width-sm))) 0 0 <color>) instead, keeping border-bottom-width a constant 1px in the box model at every state - zero layout impact. context=default uses the same technique, inset on all four sides.

Neither `.root[data-invalid='true']` nor `.context_inline[data-invalid='true']` touches border-width: both paint the thicker error line with an inset box-shadow (four-sided on context=default, bottom-only on context=inline), so there is no leftover border-width shorthand to reset and no text shift.

Hovering an invalid context=inline field keeps the error border color rather than resetting to --color-border-input, per explicit design feedback - the border-color-changing hover rule is scoped with :not([data-invalid='true']); the background-changing hover rule is not, since hover should still tint the background on an invalid field.

elemBeforeInput and elemAfterInput are separate, asymmetric Figma components (icon|text vs icon-button|button), not a symmetric before/after pair - iconBefore is always aria-hidden, iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden.
Inline padding is asymmetric per size (tighter on the end side) and the icon/input gap varies per size (4px/6px/8px) rather than a flat 6px, confirmed directly from Figma's per-side bound variables.

elemAfterInput gained a third `type` option in Figma - `label` - alongside `icon` and `button`, nesting a real Label atom instance (tone=default, emphasis=subtle, size sm/md). Since `iconAfter` is already `React.ReactNode` and `.action` is a plain centered flex wrapper, this required no component code change - only documenting the newly-supported content type.

Gained an additive leadingContent slot so Select can render multi-select chips inside the field frame without a second bordered frame or duplicated state CSS. In-frame, before the input, not aria-hidden (unlike the decorative iconBefore); shrinks/clips to keep the field single-line. Additive and opt-in - existing TextField usage is unchanged. Not derived from a TextField Figma variant; it exists to serve Select, whose own select-trigger nests chips inside its text-field instance.

antiPatterns: choosing from a fixed set of options
faking an input with a non-form element

anatomy.description: Bordered frame holding the optional before/action slots and the input; reacts to :hover, :focus-within, and the input's :autofill (via :has).
Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative - never interactive.

Optional interactive in-frame content before the input, sharing its row - added so a token/multi-select field (Select) can render removable chips inside the frame. Shrinks and clips to keep the field single-line. Unlike iconBefore, not aria-hidden.
The real native text input; carries all forwarded native attributes.
Optional trailing icon or interactive action (e.g. an IconButton clear button). Never forced aria-hidden.

size.description: Frame height, padding, gap, and typography.

context.description: default is bordered at rest, rounded on all four corners; inline has no border/background at rest, shows the raised-hover background and a 1px bottom border on hover, a 2px bottom focus/error line on focus/invalid, and always has square bottom corners - for a field inside a row, such as a search box or a Key Value Pair value. Matches Figma's context axis.

appearance.description: Deprecated - use context. subtle and inline map to context='inline', default to 'default'. Still accepted; an explicit context wins.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and the error border (thicker, regardless of focus).

iconBefore.description: Optional leading icon or short text prefix. Always decorative (aria-hidden).

iconAfter.description: Optional trailing icon or interactive control (typically an IconButton clear action, or a Button). Never forced aria-hidden.

className.description: Composes with the root frame's class list.

inputClassName.description: Composes with the native input's class list.

leadingContent.description: Interactive in-frame content between iconBefore and the input (e.g. Select's chips). Not aria-hidden; shrinks/clips to stay single-line. Existing usage is unchanged when omitted.

default.purpose: Bordered box with a raised-surface background at rest, rounded on all four corners.

inline.purpose: Chromeless at rest; raised-hover background and a 1px bottom border on hover, a 2px bottom focus/error line on focus/invalid. Keeps the field's normal padding, height, and top-corner radius; bottom corners always square. For a field inside a row, such as a search box or a Key Value Pair value.

slots.name: iconBefore
supports: a small icon from the generated icon set

slots.name: leadingContent
supports: removable Chips for a multi-select field (Select)
other interactive tokens shown ahead of the input

slots.name: iconAfter
supports: a small icon from the generated icon set
an IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) for a clear/dismiss action
a Button for a labeled action
a Label pill for compact metadata/status after the input (e.g. a unit or status tag)

color.autofill_background: --color-background-autofill-default (background-image layer over the --color-elevation-surface-raised-default background-color, both contexts)

requirements: Render a real native <input> - never fake one.
Set aria-invalid on the input when invalid is true.
iconBefore is aria-hidden - decorative only, never interactive.
iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton clear action) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.
Text Field does not manage labelling - pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby.

keyboardInteraction: Native input keyboard behavior - Tab to focus, type to enter text.
When iconAfter holds an interactive control, Tab reaches it as its own stop after the input, in native DOM order.
behaviorRules: Render a real <input> inside a bordered frame div.
The deprecated appearance prop maps to context: subtle and inline map to inline, default to default. An explicit context wins.
hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill are never props - they derive from :hover, :focus-within, :placeholder-shown, and :autofill plus the input's own value.

An autofilled field (the input matches :autofill) layers --color-background-autofill-default over the raised surface in both contexts and keeps each context's resting stroke; the tint stays through hover, focus, and invalid, and a disabled field shows its disabled look instead.
The browser's own autofill fill on the input is hidden (background-clip: text) and its forced text color replaced (-webkit-text-fill-color, caret-color), with no transition.
invalid always renders the thicker error border regardless of focus state.

The focus-frame indicator replaces the resting border color directly (:focus-within), the same pattern invalid uses, not an outline ring around it. Border-width stays a constant 1px on context=default at every state (rest, hover, focus, invalid) - focus/invalid instead paint a thicker look via box-shadow, so the text/caret never shifts horizontally.
Hover is suppressed while the field is focus/typing (:focus-within), in both contexts.
context=inline always renders square bottom corners (0 radius), regardless of size.
context=inline shows the raised-hover background and a 1px bottom border on hover.
context=inline rests at 1px border-width, the same as context=default, at every state - focus/invalid look thicker via box-shadow only, never a real border-bottom-width change.
Hover never overrides the invalid border color on context=inline - only the background changes on hover when invalid is also true.
iconBefore is icon-or-text only, always aria-hidden; iconAfter is icon-or-action, never forced aria-hidden.
compositionRules: Pair with a native label[htmlFor] or aria-label/aria-labelledby - Text Field does not include one.
Use Select instead of Text Field when the value comes from a fixed set of options.
For an interactive iconAfter clear/dismiss action, use a real IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) rather than a bare icon standing in for a button.
contentRules: Single line only - no textarea mode.
Content should match the native `type` in use.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all colors use semantic tokens.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo + React.forwardRef<HTMLInputElement> for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, radius, or typography.
Do not add a state prop - hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill are all native pseudo-class/value-driven.
do: Use the native type attribute (email, password, search, ...) for the right keyboard and built-in validation.
Pair with a native label[htmlFor] pointing at the input's id.
Use context=inline for a field inside a row - a search box, an inline-edit field, a Key Value Pair value - that shouldn't visually compete with surrounding content until interacted with.
Use a real IconButton (appearance=subtle, shape=square) for an interactive iconAfter clear/dismiss action.
dont: Do not use for multi-line content.
Do not use for a value chosen from a fixed set of options.
Do not fake an input with a styled non-form element.
Do not force aria-hidden on an interactive iconAfter control.
acceptanceCriteria: Supports all TextFieldSize and TextFieldContext values; deprecated TextFieldAppearance values map to a context.
invalid sets aria-invalid=true and the thicker error border, regardless of focus.
disabled prevents interaction and applies disabled tokens.
context=inline renders square bottom corners at every size.
context=inline rests at the same 1px border-width as context=default.
Hovering an invalid context=inline field keeps the error border color visible.
iconBefore renders as decorative (aria-hidden); iconAfter renders without a forced aria-hidden and stays focusable when it holds a real IconButton/Button.
Placeholder vs. value text color follows :placeholder-shown automatically, with no state prop.
Focus/typing replaces the resting border color/width via :focus-within, the same way invalid does.
Hover never shows while the field is focused/typing.
An autofilled field shows --color-background-autofill-default over the raised surface in both contexts, with no browser autofill fill on the input, and keeps the tint through hover and focus.
Works in light and dark themes.
Storybook includes Playground, Variants, States, Content, and Edge Cases.
Tests cover rendering, size/context, the deprecated appearance mapping, invalid, disabled, icons, interactive iconAfter accessibility, native attribute forwarding, and the autofill treatment.
knownLimitations: No multi-line mode - use Text Area.
No integrated label, helper text, or error message - Figma's source component doesn't include them; wrap it in Field.
